articles.title: Defiant DeChambeau 'grateful' for LIV, vague on future plans
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he does not regret joining LIV Golf and offered no new details of his future plans in his first public comments since the di...
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he does not regret joining LIV Golf and offered no new details of his future plans in his first public comments since the divisive tour announced it is shutting down.

DeChambeau was arguably the highest profile member of a swathe of golf stars who defected from the traditional PGA Tour to free-spending LIV in 2022, turning the golf world on its head.

The two-time US Open winner had continued to staunchly defend the rebel tour even after its Saudi backers pulled the plug this year, expressing optimism for a now-aborted "LIV 2.0" relaunch plan even as others like Jon Rahm jumped ship.

With LIV announcing on Thursday that it will shutter for good, DeChambeau issued a statement expressing gratitude for his experience with the rebel tour.

"I'm not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home," he said.

"The record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg will stick with me for the rest of my life.

"I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive."

DeChambeau expressed confidence that LIV Golf's distinctive team-based format would be successful in the future.

"I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game," he said.

Several former LIV stars have announced they will play on the DP World (European) Tour next season -- a potential route to one day returning to the US PGA Tour.

DeChambeau, whose personal commercial ventures include a hugely popular YouTube channel, did not reveal his future competitive plans, beyond a scheduled appearance at next month's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa.

But the famously outspoken and self-confident star vowed to act with "humility and respect" in the future as he ponders his next step.

"Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," he said.

"Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me."

Beyond the Nedbank Golf Challenge event, "I'll go about whatever is next the right way," he added.

articles.title: Blades Brown at 19 becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years. Rahm win in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: LOS CABOS, Mexico (AP) — Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-...
articles.body:
LOS CABOS, Mexico (AP) — Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James with a birdie on the second playoff hole in the World Wide Technology Championship.

Brown became the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his moxie by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the playoff.

But he missed an 8-foot putt on the second playoff hole, and Brown made his 3-footer.

ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Jon Rahm fought off Ryder Cup teammates Rory McIlroy and Tyrrell Hatton to win the Abu Dhabi Championship on Sunday for his first European tour title in four years and his first start since the demise of LIV Golf.

Rahm shot 5-under 67 at Yas Links and finished two shots ahead of Hatton (68) and four ahead of McIlroy (69) in the first of the two season-ending playoff tournaments in the United Arab Emirates.

This was Rahm's first event in seven weeks, during which time his wife gave birth to their fourth child and he finalized his departure from LIV Golf. The victory moves him back into the top 10 in the world ranking.

McIlroy moved to No. 2 in the Race to Dubai, 534 points behind Eugenio Chacarra. The title will be decided next week at the DP World Tour Championship, which McIlroy has won three times.

OMITAMA, Japan (AP) — Shuri Sakuma became the fifth Japanese player to win on the LPGA Tour this season, closing with an 8-under 64 for a four-shot victory in the Toto Classic.

Sakuma won for the fifth time on the Japan LPGA this year, after a four-win season in 2025. The victory makes her eligible to join the LPGA Tour. She finished at 20-under 268.

Aki Iwai, who had a one-shot lead going into the final round, closed with a 71 to finish second. Erika Hara finished a career-best third after a 70 at the Taiheiyo Club north of Tokyo, moving Hara to No. 32 in the Race to CME Globe.

Yuta Ikeda closed with a 4-under 67l and won a three-man playoff to capture the ACN Championship on the Japan Tour. Ikeda won after Kohei Okada made bogey on the first playoff hole, and Ryunosoke Furukawa Kohei failed to match Ikeda's par on the fourth playoff hole. ... Ana Pelaez Trivino rallied from five shots behind with a 9-under 64, winning the Aramco China Championship by three shots over Mimi Rhodes on the Ladies European Tour. ... Louis Albertse closed with a 4-under 68 for a three-shot victory in the Telkom PGA Championship on the Sunshine Tour in South Africa. ... Jean Hugo closed with a 7-under 65 to win the European Senior Masters in Spain for his third win in as many starts on the Legends Tour. ... Hyunjo Yoo shot 4-under 68 and won the Daebo HausD Championship by one shot on the Korea LPGA.

images.caption: FILE - Blades Brown celebrates a birdie putt at the 18th green during the third round of the American Express golf event on the Pete Dye Stadium Course at PGA West, Jan. 24, 2026, in La Quinta, Calif. (AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin, File) (AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin)

Jon Rahm of Spain poses with the championship trophy after winning the Abu Dhabi Golf Championship in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Altaf Qadri) (AP Photo/Altaf Qadri)

articles.title: 49ers ride takeaways, effective ground game to win over Raiders and 7-1 record
articles.summary: The 49ers got three interceptions and two fumble recoveries from the defense and the offense had 190 yards rushing in their win over the Raiders at Levi's St...
articles.body:
On a day in which the San Francisco 49ers ' new-look defensive line largely struggled to generate pressure, it was the back end of the defense that created action.

The 49ers, who beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday at Levi's Stadium, entered the day with seven takeaways in seven games. On Sunday, they had five - all in the second half - during a stretch of complete domination for that unit. A Las Vegas offense led by quarterback Kirk Cousins, despite having plenty of opportunities to cut its deficit to one possession while the 49ers' offense struggled out of the half, repeatedly gave the ball away.

The results of the Raiders' opening five drives after halftime: pick-six, touchdown, fumble, fumble, interception.

San Francisco owes much of that to its trio of starting linebackers. Rookie Jaden Dugger took the first play of the second half to the house. Two drives later, Fred Warner punched the ball out at the 26-yard line (his fifth forced fumble of the season) and Dre Greenlaw recovered at the 31. On the ensuing possession, defensive back Upton Stout did his best Warner impression, punching the ball free from Raiders tight end Michael Mayer's grasp as he extended into the end zone; Warner recovered, keeping Las Vegas from cutting its deficit to four.

On the next drive, San Francisco's defense looked to be in trouble again. A 33-yard completion to tight end Brock Bowers brought the Raiders to the 1-yard line. Cousins attempted a quarterback sneak, and Warner dove over the pile to knock him back two yards. Two plays later, cornerback Renardo Green leaped to intercept a ball intended for Tre Tucker in the right corner of the end zone. Safety Malik Mustapha added an interception for good measure in garbage time.

Not a bad stretch for defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' unit.

SF: McCaffrey 1 run (Pineiro kick), 9:32.

SF: McCaffrey 12 pass from Purdy (Pineiro kick), 5:14.

SF: Dugger 35 interception return (Pineiro kick), 14:43.

Las: Bowers 21 pass from Cousins (Gay kick), 9:29.

SF: Watkins 37 pass from Purdy (Pineiro kick), :36.

RUSHING: Las Vegas, Jeanty 6-25, Bowers 1-2, Cousins 2-0, Washington 6-(minus 3). San Francisco, Black 11-70, McCaffrey 18-68, Purdy 7-40, James 3-11, Juszczyk 1-4, Jones 3-(minus 3).

PASSING: Las Vegas, Cousins 22-32-3-216. San Francisco, Purdy 17-25-1-232.

RECEIVING: Las Vegas, Bowers 7-111, Jeanty 5-(minus 5), Tucker 4-55, Mayer 3-37, Nailor 2-9, Bech 1-9. San Francisco, Watkins 4-86, Kittle 4-58, Robinson 3-22, Cooks 2-25, McCaffrey 2-19, Hodge 1-17, Cowing 1-5.

Run, run the ball: The Raiders entered Sunday allowing a league-worst 5.1 yards per rushing attempt. They gave up 365 yards on the ground in their previous two games entering Sunday. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan was well aware of this fact, telling the Fox broadcast pregame he was aiming to have a 40-carry game.

San Francisco ended the afternoon with a season-high of 43 runs, with the caveat that a number of those came on the game's final drive with the result sealed.

The 49ers managed 25 rushes in the first half alone, gaining 125 yards on the ground for two touchdowns. Quarterback Brock Purdy threw the ball only 12 times before the break, averaging 10.3 yards per attempt for 123 yards.

In the second half, the 49ers strayed a bit from that strategy. Twelve rushes to 13 passes to start the period was a far cry from the first-half ratio, but San Francisco still managed to gain 4.4 yards per rush and 190 yards on the ground.

Purdy alone racked up a season-high 40 rushing yards on seven attempts and scored a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey ran 18 times for 68 yards and a score, and rookie backup Kaelon Black toted the ball 11 times for 70 yards.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Delivers Blunt Assessment of Drake Maye After Patriots Loss
articles.summary: The Patriots quarterback threw three interceptions in a four-turnover loss to Green Bay.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots had a night to forget against the Green Bay Packers, and head coach Mike Vrabel didn't try to sugarcoat it.

New England committed four turnovers in its Week 9 loss, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions. Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but his turnovers put the Patriots in an early hole and made it difficult to keep pace with Green Bay.

"We lost, and we got our asses kicked," Vrabel told reporters after the game. "There's no two ways around it. Like, that's what happened tonight."

The Patriots coach pointed to several areas that need improvement, including tackling, pressuring the quarterback and creating turnovers defensively. He also stressed the importance of maintaining offensive balance rather than becoming too reliant on the passing game when trailing.

Maye's performance was a significant part of the problem. Vrabel admitted he was disappointed by how the quarterback's afternoon unfolded.

"I'm surprised about, you know, just the way that the day went, the way that it started, and then I guess kind of how the third quarter went," Vrabel said.

Maye took responsibility for his mistakes, acknowledging that his turnovers put the defense in difficult positions and prevented the offense from building momentum.

"Starting with me, man, it's one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games," Maye said. "And so, you know, our defense in a bad spot, you know, in the first drive. And just, you know, gave them the football."

The quarterback also admitted he was late on some throws and needed to do a better job with his decision-making and communication.

"I'm sure disappointed in myself. You can't put the team in the hole, you know, straight off the bat," Maye said. "And we had chances to, you know, put us back within three points, you know, multiple times. And just frustrating."

Despite the disappointing result, Vrabel emphasized that the Patriots need to move forward together and show how they'll respond.

"Losing is frustrating," Vrabel said. "We're in this together. We're going to get them back and get ready to travel and put 48 guys out there that care and want to exhibit some sort of identity, and see how we respond."

articles.title: Jon Rahm Wins $1.5 Million but Still Down $100 Million from LIV
articles.summary: Jon Rahm won his first tournament after leaving LIV Golf, earning $1.53 million while still owed over $100 million by the collapsed league.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm secured his first tournament victory since departing LIV Golf on Sunday, claiming the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship with a final score of 23-under par. The Spanish golfer finished two strokes ahead of Tyrrell Hatton and four shots clear of Rory McIlroy at Yas Links. This win marks a return to form for Rahm, who had not won on the DP World Tour since November 2022. Despite the triumph, the financial reality of his exit remains stark: he forfeited over $100 million in potential earnings by leaving the breakaway circuit.

The Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship offered a total purse of $9 million, with Rahm taking home the winner's check of $1.53 million. According to Celebrity Net Worth, this prize money represents only about 1.43 percent of the funds LIV Golf still owed him at the time of his departure. The league, which declared bankruptcy and officially folded this year, had promised massive payouts to its top players. Rahm was the league's individual champion in each of its seasons, yet he chose to walk away from the guaranteed money when the terms of a potential LIV 2.0 became unacceptable.

Rahm's victory on Sunday followed a seven-week break that saw the birth of his second daughter and his final departure from the now-defunct LIV Golf league. The Spaniard admitted that mental battles and external distractions had hampered his recent play leading up to this event. "After everything that's gone on," Rahm said, according to Yahoo Sports , "and some poor play and some battles mentally with a lot of noise, to come back out after a bit of rest and being with the family, it's quite special." His last regular-tour win on the European circuit came at the World Tour Championship in November 2022, just before his controversial move to the Saudi-backed league.

Three birdies across five holes beginning at the 11th hole allowed Rahm to surge ahead, demanding precision and patience in the final round for victory. He shot a 5-under 67 to finish the week, while Hatton carded a 68 and McIlroy posted a 69. Rahm described his performance on the final day as nearly perfect despite a single error. "As far as I'm concerned, except the (tee) shot on No. 17, I played a pretty flawless round," said Rahm, who banked a winner's check of $1.5 million. "It was really, really something." This result propelled him from 51st to sixth in the overall Race to Dubai standings.

The top two finishers at the Abu Dhabi event were both former LIV Golf members, signaling a potential trend of players returning to established tours after the breakaway circuit's collapse. Tyrrell Hatton, who finished second and earned $990,000, had played with Rahm on the Legion XIII team during the LIV era. Rory McIlroy, who finished third and took home $563,000, has been one of the most vocal critics of LIV Golf throughout its existence. The presence of these high-profile players suggests the DP World Tour is regaining its competitive depth as the alternative league winds down operations.

Winning the Race to Dubai title remains possible for Rahm next week if he secures victory at the DP World Tour Championship. This singular win has already demonstrated his ability to compete at the highest level without the financial guarantees of his previous contract. While he may never fully recoup the $100 million he left on the table, the win proves his game remains sharp. DP World Tour leadership and the circuit itself are expected to receive a major boost from his return to European golf in 2027.

The financial toll of Rahm's decision remains a defining aspect of his career transition. Reports indicate the league owed him $7 million in unpaid wages, and his departure cost him an additional $100 million in future guarantees. According to Celebrity Net Worth, Rahm accepted the decision to leave all that money behind and separate from LIV Golf. The league's funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ended earlier this year, leading to a rapid unraveling of the organization's financial structure. With the league now bankrupt, Rahm's decision to leave before the final collapse may have saved his long-term reputation despite the immediate cash loss.

Rahm's performance on Sunday confirms he is ready to rebuild his legacy on the traditional tours. "From last to first is a pretty good feeling," he told reporters here in Abu Dhabi, referencing his rapid ascent in the standings, according to Today's Golfer . With a new life stage approaching, the Spaniard has once again become one of the world's top golfers. This victory is a strong start to his post-LIV career, even if the financial debt from the breakaway league remains unpaid. The DP World Tour now has a major star competing in its season-ending events.
